clue.text: Indulging in fantasies to win over party on left

indicators.note: on says the left-hand letter sits directly against the party word, ahead of it

parts.note: to woo someone is to try to win them over
a gathering is a social get-together, a party

explanation.surface: A daydreamer wins over a left-wing party only in their imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks political in the surface, but it is just the letter L, and 'on' places it hard against the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolgathering is idle daydreaming, letting the mind wander through fancies.

clue.text: Switch positions? I'm not sure it's available

parts.note: the two settings of a switch are on and off
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Someone flicking a switch wonders aloud whether something is available.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods on offer are being offered for sale, so obtainable.

clue.text: Religious book very fortunate to lose its covers

indicators.note: covers are the outside letters, so the first and last are dropped from the synonym

parts.note: fluky (also flukey) means lucky through sheer chance

explanation.surface: A precious scripture is lucky to survive though it has lost its binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke is the third Gospel, a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: A number welcoming opening of tennis courts

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: an aria is a number, a song, in an opera

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A group of players starts using the tennis courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courtyards of Roman houses, plural of atrium.

clue.text: The euro struggles to maintain rating in this area

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the scrambled letters hold the rating inside
the euro struggling suggests its letters thrashing about into a new order

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: A currency battles to keep its credit rating locally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggles' rearranges the letters of THE EURO, and 'to maintain' wraps them round the naval rating. 'rating' tempts as a credit score, but an able seaman is a rating in the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereabout means near this place, an adverb of location.

clue.text: Hearing papal take on sex, I hold things together

definitions.note: the answer speaks of itself in the first person; the definition is a noun phrase in disguise

indicators.note: hearing means the phrase is judged by how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: the Pope's ruling against condoms: rubber banned

explanation.surface: A listener hears the Vatican's view on sex and claims to keep things united.
explanation.walkthrough: The Catholic Church forbids contraception, so 'rubber' (slang for a condom) is 'banned'.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastic loop's job is to keep bundles of items bound.

clue.text: Vagrant in hedge made a beastly sound

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: A tramp sleeping in a hedgerow lets out an animal noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vagrant' looks like the tramp, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse neighs, a cry of an animal or beast.

clue.text: Person who disses rapper?

definitions.meaning: a persistent critic who runs things down
the question mark flags the music meaning as a decoy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the critic insulting people is a hip-hop artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A door knocker strikes or raps, and to knock is to belittle.

clue.text: Stops doing more acid to provide impetus

parts.note: to kick a habit is to stop doing it
tarter means sourer, more acidic

explanation.surface: Quitting heavier LSD use gives someone a fresh drive in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acid' looks like the drug, but here it means sour.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickstarter is whatever gets something going, a boost or spur.

clue.text: Cause friction again with hot pants

parts.note: to rub is to create friction
bis, from Latin, is a musical direction to repeat
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Someone rubs a pair of hot trousers again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for nonsense or poor quality, not underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang both words mean worthless or very bad.

clue.text: He dispensed treatment in Post Office Boxes

parts.note: in means fashionable, as does hip
crates are boxes

explanation.surface: A doctor handed out medicines inside post office boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it supplies HIP, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocrates was the ancient Greek physician, father of medicine.

clue.text: Part of shirt collar, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the band at the end of a shirt sleeve
to collar is to arrest, and to ... is to handcuff a suspect, so collaring is an example

explanation.definitionFit: A cuff ends a sleeve, and police cuff a prisoner they arrest.

clue.text: Duchess eats half of rare meat, which is a blow

indicators.note: eating takes food inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: Kate Middleton was Duchess of Cambridge

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

parts.note: a chop is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: A royal duchess eating underdone meat is shocking news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is a' links wordplay to definition; 'a blow' tempts as bad news.
explanation.definitionFit: A karate chop is a sharp strike with the side of the hand.

clue.text: Dull-witted American president's thrown outside

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters go around the other piece
thrown suggests the letters tossed into disorder

parts.note: president's read as 'president is'; the word president is the fodder

explanation.surface: A slow American head of state has been ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' rearranges PRESIDENT and 'outside' puts it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian means plodding, lacking imagination or flair.

clue.text: Germany's current period of overindulgence

definitions.meaning: a bout of unrestrained spending or drinking

explanation.definitionFit: The Spree is Berlin's river, and a binge is a spree.

clue.text: Clue for mystery solver on TV

definitions.meaning: in rhyming slang ... means clue, as in 'not a Scooby'
The cartoon Great Dane who solves mysteries

explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang turns clue into the cartoon detective dog's name.

clue.text: Decent trousers in golf, it appears

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the word takes the other letters inside

parts.note: seemly means proper, decent
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Respectable trousers are what golfers wear, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like clothing but is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemingly means apparently, by appearances.

clue.text: Paying chaps to stuff when it may be lunch time

definitions.note: paying is used as a noun here, the act of paying for wrongdoing

indicators.note: to stuff is to fill, so these letters are pushed inside the others

parts.note: lunch might be at one o'clock
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men are paid to fill up on food at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends, paying the price for a wrong.

clue.text: Funny bloke is something to see in Paris

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters go peculiar and reorder

explanation.surface: A comic man is a tourist attraction in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luxor obelisk stands in the Place de la Concorde, a Parisian sight.

clue.text: Sailors seizing princess on stage twirling bottom

indicators.note: twirling spins the whole thing round, so it is read backwards
seizing means grabbing, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
Princess Ida is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta

explanation.surface: Seamen grab a royal on stage who is spinning her rear end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' puts the princess inside the sailors, and 'twirling' turns the result round. Princess Ida is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, hence 'on stage'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the rock bottom.

clue.text: Record covered by Erasure is so damn uplifting!

indicators.note: uplifting says the hidden letters are read backwards
covered by means the answer lies under these words, held within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fan raves that a song by the synth-pop band Erasure is wonderfully cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'covered' into the definition, but 'covered by' is the indicator that the answer is concealed; the definition is 'Record'. In a down clue, 'uplifting' reads REISSOD bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of documents, a record on a subject.

clue.text: Showy Kafka work keeps a chapter apart

indicators.note: apart says the two inserted pieces go in separate places
keeps means holds, so the novel's title takes letters inside

parts.note: The Trial is Franz Kafka's novel

explanation.surface: A flamboyant production of a Kafka novel separates out one chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' and 'apart' together say the novel's title holds the A and the C in two different places rather than as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical means exaggerated, done for dramatic display.

clue.text: Fighter catches Greek priestess dressing

indicators.note: catches means grabs hold of, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the boxer
Io was a priestess of Hera in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A warrior seizes a priestess of ancient Greece as she gets dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' looks like putting on clothes, but it is the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise served as a sauce or dressing.

clue.text: It demands attention in extremely pompous way

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: St, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Something insists on being noticed in a very self-important manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hissed sound used to catch someone's notice.

clue.text: Inclination to put butter on starter of pancakes

indicators.note: in a down entry, on puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a ram butts, so it is a butter

indicators.note: a word's starter is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone feels inclined to spread butter on the first pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the spread but 'one who butts', a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a slope, an incline.

clue.text: Fulminating in a bad way, Republican takes lead

indicators.note: taking the lead means going in front of the other piece

parts.note: ailing means sickly, in a bad way

explanation.surface: An unwell Republican rages as he leads the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Railing means ranting, protesting bitterly against something.

clue.text: Nothing is mutable in these organs

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing
something mutable varies, changes

explanation.surface: Nothing ever stays the same in these body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovaries are the female reproductive organs.

clue.text: Softly dancing in dressy pink clothes, they've no costumes

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here: the scrambled letters dress, wrap round, the soft letter
dancing letters move about into a new order

parts.note: P, piano, means softly in music

explanation.surface: Quiet dancing goes on in smart pink outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges IN DRESSY PINK and 'clothes' wraps it round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny-dippers swim naked, without swimwear.
